## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r}
mydata <- read.csv("data.csv")
summary(mydata)
```
```{r}
plot(cars$speed, cars$dist,
     main = "Speed vs Stopping Distance",
     xlab = "Speed (mph)",
     ylab = "Distance (ft)",
     col = "blue",
     pch = 19)
```
```{r}
hist(cars$speed, main = "histogram of speed", xlab = "speed")
boxplot(cars$dist, main = "Boxplot of distance", ylab = "distance")
```

### Data structure (Vectors, Factors, Lists, Data frame, matrix and arrays)
### Vector: The foundational R data structure
###Numeric

###example
```{r}
x<-c(0.5, 0.6)
age<-c(20,35,32,29)
summary(age)
```
### Example 2
```{r}
Age<-c(35,24,18,24)
mean(Age)
```
###Logical
```{r}
x<-c(True,False)
x<-c(T,F)
```
### Character
```{r}
x<-c("a", "b", "c")
class<-c("M","F","F","M")
```
### Integer

```{r}
x <- 9:29 
```
### Complex
```{r}
x <- c(1+0i, 2+4i)
```
### Matrix and operation within matrices
```{r}
(x <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2, ncol = 3))
```
```{r}
(x <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2, ncol = 3))
```
```{r}
x%*%y
```
```{r}
(x<-list(1,"a",TRUE, 1+2i))
```
###Factor
```{r}
x<- factor(c("yes","yes","no","yes"))
```
### Create a vector with NAs in it
```{r}
x<- c(1, 2, NA, 10, 3)
```
### Return a logical vector indicating which elements are NA
```{r}
is.na(x)
```
```{r}
x<- c(1,2,4,"NA",5)
bad<-is.na(c)
print(x)
```
## What if there are multiple R objects and you want to take the subset with no missing values in any of those objects?

```{r}
x<-c(1,2,NA,4,NA,5)
y<-c("a", "b",NA,"d",NA,"f")
good<- complete.cases(x, y)
good
```
## Create a data frame
```{r}
StudentID<- c(1,2,3,4,5)
Math_score<- c(12,17,10,9,NA)
Gender<- c("M","F","M","M","F")
IT_score<-c(13,18,11,10,19)
scoredata<-data.frame(StudentID,Math_score,Gender,IT_score)
scoredata
```
## Create data from keyboard
```{r}
data_class2<-data.frame(height=numeric(0), weight=numeric(0), BMI=numeric(0))
data_class2<-edit(data_class2)
```
view(data_class2)
